title: `sqlparse.split` breaks an inline `WITH FUNCTION ... BEGIN ... END` at the semicolons inside the body
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

A query that defines an inline function with a `BEGIN ... END` body is split at every `;` inside that body.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = """WITH
FUNCTION meaning_of_life()
  RETURNS tinyint
  BEGIN
    DECLARE a tinyint DEFAULT CAST(6 as tinyint);
    DECLARE b tinyint DEFAULT CAST(7 as tinyint);
    RETURN a * b;
  END
SELECT meaning_of_life();"""
sqlparse.split(sql)
```
Expected: one statement containing everything from `WITH` to `SELECT meaning_of_life();`
Actual: four statements, the first ending after the first `DECLARE` and the last being `'END\nSELECT meaning_of_life();'`.

Semicolons inside a `BEGIN ... END` block must not end the statement, also when the statement does not start with `CREATE`. A bare `BEGIN;` is a transaction start, not a block, so `sqlparse.split('BEGIN; UPDATE t SET a = 1; COMMIT;')` must still give three statements.
acceptance: The reported query splits into exactly one statement
`BEGIN;` used as a transaction statement still splits normally
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
